name: Antfarm Architect
description: Watch a colony of simulated ants discover and excavate a procedurally generated underground world — tunnels bloom in real time as the ants follow pheromone trails. Tap anywhere to drop a food source and redirect the swarm. At any moment, tap 'Snapshot' to get your colony's personality verdict: 'The Paranoid Hoarders', 'The Tunnel Maximalists', 'The Chaotic Scouts'.

name: Antipode
description: A one-touch rotation-dodge game inspired by Duet. Control two opposing balls — one red, one blue — that orbit a fixed center point. Rotate them left or right (arrow keys / tap-and-hold) to weave both balls past falling obstacles. One hit and you start over.

name: Are You AI or Human?
description: A behavioral vibe-check that analyzes your answers to 10 absurd prompts and delivers a verdict on whether you have more human or AI energy — complete with a percentage score and a funny archetype like 'Corporate Chatbot Soul' or 'Chaotic Human NPC'. Seeded randomness ensures your specific answers always produce the same result.

name: Attention Span Colosseum
description: Hold completely still for 10 seconds. How zen are you? Tracks cumulative mouse/touch movement and assigns an archetype from Zen Master to Human Earthquake.

name: Aurora Forecast for One
pitch: Pulls today's real Kp-index and solar wind speed from NOAA's no-key feed, runs the numbers against your declared hometown's geomagnetic latitude (one input: city), and renders a personal aurora odds card: 'Tonight in Oslo: 11% odds, glowing on the northern horizon at 23:14 local.' Re-renders nightly with deterministic seed = date+city. A watch-it-glow simulation animates a ribbon over your skyline silhouette.
rationale: Lands in observe/simulation (0 archived, 1 live). Live-data-substrate concept — uses real public NOAA SWPC feed (no-key, CORS-safe). City input transforms a generic feed into an 'about me' artifact. Sidesteps the heavily-archived observe/archetype-reveal cell entirely. Single screen, single input — no wizard-stack risk. Awe arousal (scale, transformation). Reproducible without web-search proxy because the NOAA feed is deterministic per-day. Share card is screenshot-friendly: silhouette + glowing ribbon + your-city-tonight headline.

name: Boids Flock Painter
description: A canvas where a flock of 200 birds (boids) follows classic separation/alignment/cohesion rules. The user places colored 'seed' attractors by tapping or clicking — the flock swoops toward each one and leaves a glowing paint trail behind it. Each session produces a unique procedural painting shaped entirely by where the user taps. A 'Save my painting' button exports the canvas as a full-resolution image. No win state — pure hypnotic emergent art.

name: Bounce Pool
description: A daily one-shot pool puzzle. Drag from the cue ball to aim — the trajectory line is fully visible with up to three wall/bumper ricochets, so the puzzle is pure reasoning, not reflex. Clear all 5 targets in the fewest shots; par is 3. Same curated level for every player, every day. Share artifact is a compact emoji-grid plus a 'play today's level' CTA. Aesthetic: high-contrast pool-hall green felt with a chunky monospace stat overlay — not default modern app design.

name: Bug Catalogue
description: A tap-game creative-artifact in the form of a 19th-century entomologist's display case. The user is shown an empty pinning board for 30 seconds while pixel-art bugs of wildly invented species crawl/fly across the screen at varying speeds and trajectories — a gold-banded clock-roach, a translucent moth with stained-glass wings, a tiny six-legged thing carrying a cigarette. Tap a bug to pin it (gentle squelch sound, paper-thump). Catch up to 6. At time-up, the user's caught specimens snap into a riso-printed museum collection plate: each insect labeled with a deterministic latin binomial seeded from the species id and the user's catch-time, plus a one-line deadpan field note from the curator ("Specimen 03 — *Coleoptera misericordia*, captured 14:32 — known to overshadow conversations about feelings"). The plate IS the share artifact: stained sepia paper, hand-engraved illustration style, brass corner stamps. No verdict, no quiz; the catalogue is a personal museum the user assembled. Daily seed determines which species appear today, so two players' boards differ-but-rhyme.

name: Bureau of the Current Minute
pitch: A solid-color page with one line of typewritten copy and a postage-stamp date+time. The line is a hand-curated micro-decree about *this exact minute* — 'minute 3:47 PM on a Wednesday, the kind of minute where someone's microwave has been at 0:01 for thirty seconds.' Each minute of each weekday has its own pinned line (10,080 lines, hand-written in the cursed-mundane Petty-Small-Claims voice). Wait one minute: the page silently updates to the next minute's decree. Share button captures the current minute's stamped card.
rationale: No-input reveals are flagged in ai-pitfalls as risky, but the documented failure mode is invisible-anchor — and this app makes the anchor (minute, hour, weekday) the *largest visual element*, exactly satisfying the rule. The shelf has Fortune Vending (daily, pinned to date) but no minute-pinned shape — a finer-grained anchor is genuinely novel. The hand-curated 10,080-line corpus is itself a 'Proof of Human' move (it cannot plausibly be LLM-generated without obvious tells, and that becomes part of the marketing). Caption: 'the minute I opened my coffee was Bureau-classified as Section 4-Wednesday'. Risk: minute-bound reveal lowers re-share velocity (you can't show a friend *this* minute live, only your screenshot of it) — mitigation is treating screenshots as the canonical share format with the timestamp as proof. Differs from the rejected sundown-line (which was ambient observation with no caption-worthy reveal); this has a stamped, archetype-shaped, hand-written verdict per minute.
description: A federal bureau of the present tense — wait one minute, the page silently files a typewritten decree about this exact minute on a stamped, shareable card.

name: Captain's Log, Stardate Today
pitch: Pick from three drifting situations on the bridge ('the cook is hoarding the last lemons again', 'long-range sensors picked up a song'), then tap through a five-beat scene of crew responses. At the end the ship's computer renders today's Captain's Log entry in your voice — a single short page, dated to the real stardate (year + day-of-year), with the picked beats woven in. Same situation + same day = same log; different picks visibly rewrite it.
rationale: navigate/letter-narrative is sparse (1 archived, 0 live) and letter-narrative as a row is under-built outside text-input. Reframes 'sci-fi captain's log' as a discrete-choice navigation through bridge beats — passes the opaque-input causality test because each tap is a labeled choice, not a free gesture. The LLM is central but bounded by the deterministic beat picks (not a chat surface, not 'configure-to-prompt-builder' — there's accumulated state across taps), and the daily stardate anchor satisfies the no-input-reveal pinning rule. Caption-friendly: 'I am the captain who befriended the singing nebula today.' Identity-job under Ze Frank's taxonomy.

name: Cartograph Duel
pitch: Two friends join via room code and race to draw the outline of a country from memory. Closest to the real shape wins. Best of 3.
rationale: The multiplayer cell is nearly empty (only Reflex Duel II is active). Pairs BuzzFeed's friend-callout connection job with a draw mechanic — a pairing nowhere in the portfolio. Solo-UAT-able via two-phone test. Drawing from memory sidesteps the 'drawing apps are about pretty output' trap; it's a competence flex with a clean win condition. Geometric overlap scoring is deterministic — no AI, no copyrighted assets.
description: Two friends join via room code and race to draw the outline of a country from memory. Closest to the real shape wins. Best of 3.

name: Catch of the Day
description: A 30-second pixel-art fishing minigame: tap to cast, then a tension meter wobbles as a hidden fish fights the line — release at the right moment, mistime it twice and the fish breaks free. Six measurable catch traits (cast distance, tension peaks, fight duration, line-snap near-misses, reel rhythm, time-of-bite) deterministically condition both a named species and an illustrated portrait. The reveal is a tri-folded Naturalist's Field Plate from the fictional 'Lake Verity Survey' — generated fish illustration centered as Exhibit A in 1830s scientific-plate style (etched cross-hatching, faded sepia paper, latin binomial), with HTML/CSS overlays for the species name ('Glass-Toothed Drift Carp'), behavioral notes quoting your specific catch ('fought for 7s with two surface breaches'), conservation status, and a deadpan field-naturalist's quote.

name: Closer to 1.000
pitch: Hold a button for as close to 1.000 seconds as you can. The closer you get, the more people you beat. On release, your hold lands as a pin on the live curve of every hold ever submitted (real aggregation, served by a shared histogram Lambda) and you get a percentile + tier (BULLSEYE / DEAD-ON / SHARP / CLOSE / LOOSE / WIDE / OFF). Three holds per session, one combined best-of-three score, URL-fragment encoded share. The histogram was bootstrapped with 1,500 synthetic samples (Laplace, scale ~120ms) so the percentile reads meaningfully on day one; real plays accumulate on top and dilute the seed naturally as traffic grows.
rationale: Single-button / single-second-constraint apps are the format of the moment (Lizard Button is currently viral) and the live shelf has nothing in this lane — it has reflex games (Reflex Duel II) and casual taps (Tap to Wake the Cat) but nothing built on the inability-to-hold-an-exact-duration as the comedy mechanic. The constraint itself is funny: humans cannot hold a button for exactly 1.000s and they know it, so every result feels like the button caught them. Honest framing as fortune-keyed-by-input passes the input-resolution rule. Confession bank must be hand-written, not LLM (200 lines is tractable, all flattering-or-cursed-but-never-shaming). Solo-UAT-perfect: each confession is its own caption, three holds per session means three shareable artifacts. Caption-test: 'the button knows' is the franchise-line. Mitigation for bank-size: bake a per-day rotation index into the bin lookup so the same bin returns different lines on different days.
description: Hold a button for as close to 1.000 seconds as you can. Each hold pins on a distribution curve and tells you what % of attempts you beat. Three holds per session, share your best-of-three.

name: Closing Argument: Yourself v. Yourself
pitch: One single-sentence input: name a stupid thing you keep doing ('checking my ex's spotify', 'opening the fridge twice in 4 minutes', 'replying to slack at 11pm'). Pick a chip for which side gets to go first (PROSECUTION or DEFENSE). The app generates a 4-section mock court transcript — opening statement, three pieces of damning evidence the prosecution submits, the defense's rebuttal, and the judge's verdict (with sentence) — all rendered as a stamped 'STATE OF [YOUR FIRST NAME] v. [YOUR FIRST NAME]' court filing. The system auto-absurdifies the dollar amount of the fine ($3.88, etc.), the user never picks numbers.
rationale: Direct extension of the petty-small-claims winner — one of the factory's pre-validated benign-violation templates. Single sentence + one chip = no recall-from-life, no paragraph-labor, no wizard depth (passes all the strengthened input rules from this week's deprecations). Input is already the funny part the user wrote; configuration shapes the verdict from the system side. Auto-absurdify rule respected (system picks the dollar amount, not the user). Arousal: amusement + petty-anger (spite handle). Verdict-desirability passes — every verdict is mock-shameful in a flattering way ('I got a $4.12 fine for opening the fridge twice'). Mock-legal-document stance carries the Form dimension (Shifman: stamps + 'STATE OF X' is instantly recognizable as the same template across users). Wrapper test passes via 4-section structure (multiple derived sections from one input). Caption: 'I just lost a court case to myself.' Avoids sci-fi register the user rejected three times today.

name: Cold Case File #
pitch: You're handed a fake unsolved-mystery case file. Click through 4 evidence pages (witness statement, photo, lab note, timeline) — each click marks one piece of evidence as 'corroborates' or 'contradicts.' Your decisions print an Official Detective Profile certificate naming your investigative archetype (e.g., 'Hunch-Driven Beat Detective,' 'Paper-Trail Pedant') with a closure-rate stamp.
rationale: Lands in navigate/document-cert (1 live / 1 archived — fresh). Sidesteps the bare archetype-reveal watchlist by delivering a document-shaped certificate. High arousal: anxiety + curiosity (commit before reveal). Every detective archetype is owned, not judged. Hand-authored case content is deterministic so the verdict feels eerily tailored to the specific click trail. No wizard stack — all clicks happen inside one continuous interactive case file.

name: Console Pilot
pitch: Hold your phone like a yoke and tilt to fly your one-person scout through a procedurally generated nebula corridor. No menus — just pitch/roll/yaw against drifting debris and signal beacons. End-of-run you get a one-page Flight Recorder card: max-G, closest-pass distance, sector traversed, and a callsign the ship christens you ('Cmdr. Shortwave', 'Pilot 4-Echo-Twitchy').
rationale: tilt-rotate/score is a totally unsaturated cell (0:1 currently) and sci-fi piloting is the most physically intuitive mapping for device orientation — pose-zero, monotonic, one-step metaphor are all natural. Pure on-device JS (three.js or canvas), no LLM, no API risk. Arousal is high (real-time motion + near-misses); the share artifact is a flight recorder card with a callsign verdict so the result is a name, not a number. Solo-UAT-able and passes the native-app-genre check because tilt steering is a web-native modality, not a port of an app-store endless-runner.

No menus — just pitch/roll/yaw against drifting debris and signal beacons. name: Constellation Maker
description: Click anywhere on a dark starfield canvas to place stars. Connect them to draw your own constellation. When you're done, press 'Name It' — the app uses the shape's geometry (centroid, arm count, density) to deterministically assign a poetic constellation name and a one-sentence myth. Download a shareable image of your named constellation.

name: Court of Public Reaction
pitch: A 60-second pixel-art live 'performance' plays out on a tiny stage on screen — a deadpan stand-up bit, a sweating magician, a defendant pleading their case, rotated daily. You are the audience. As the bit unfolds in real time, you tap one of five reaction chips: POLITE LAUGH / GASP / BOO / SLOW CLAP / WALK OUT. Crucially, the performer visibly reacts to you in real time — the comedian sweats and re-paces when you don't laugh; the magician freezes mid-trick when you boo; the defendant stares directly at you when you slow-clap. At the curtain, the performer breaks character, walks to the front, and reads your reaction pattern back as a stamped Critic's Notice: 'you are the kind of audience that gasps three beats before the punchline. Recommended seat: Row K, near the exit. Verdict: PRE-EMPTIVE GASPER, MILDLY CURSED.' Same daily performance for everyone. Share is the Critic's Notice, with your timing graph as evidence.
rationale: Direct corrective for the Reality TV Reaction Engine deprecation (May 2). That app failed because it was 'tap chips at scrolling moments' with no on-stage feedback — the textbook opaque-input-mechanic causality failure from design-voice. This closes the loop: the performer reacting in real time IS the causality teacher (the explicit remediation that page prescribes). No other app on the shelf has the user-as-audience-judging-tiny-live-performer shape. Sidesteps the recently-fatal observe-app graveyard (Specimen Drift, Tank Verdict, Tide Diviner, Tonight's Sky, Sundown Line, The Walking Tour all archived in the past two weeks) by giving the user real authorship — taps demonstrably steer what happens on stage. Sidesteps the wrapper-shape critique because the LLM is bounded: only the final Critic's Notice copy is generated, and it's branched off discrete reaction-timing data, not a free prompt. Arousal mix: amusement (the absurd bits) + anxiety (did I boo too early?) + curiosity (what is this performer about to do). Verdict-desirability: every audience archetype is shareable (Pre-Emptive Gasper, Polite-Boo Pacifist, Confused Slow-Clapper, Late-Laugher). Job-to-be-done stack: humor + identity + connection. Risk: the performer's reactivity must be visible enough to teach the causality without overriding the bit — solved by 4–5 subtle distinct stress states (sweat, re-pace, freeze, glance at exit) keyed to tap rhythm. Differentiates from FOBO Simulator (non-reactive sprite getting replaced) and from passive observe apps.

name: Crowd Simulator
description: Draw walls, place exits, release the crowd. Can you engineer a perfect escape?

name: Cryptid Sighting Report
description: A 3-question intake (location type, time of day, what you think you saw) that generates an official 'Cryptid Field Classification Report' from a fake government agency — complete with a named cryptid species, threat level, behavioral notes, and a cartoonish pixelated cryptid illustration via the image proxy. Tone: deadpan field-guide seriousness. Aesthetic: faded typewriter form, government-agency letterhead, red classification stamps.

name: Cursed Trading Card
description: User types a short free-text "creature concept" (e.g. "gas station mystic", "overcaffeinated raccoon CEO"). The app calls the AI text proxy to invent a name, type, attack/defense stats, and a one-line absurd flavor lore, then calls the image proxy for a hand-painted illustration of the creature. The frontend overlays the name + stats + lore on a vintage 1990s collectible-card frame (foil border, holo gradient, watermark). The card is downloadable as PNG and shareable via URL fragment that re-renders the same card text (image is regenerated on share-load since image-proxy can't echo bytes through a URL).

name: Dead Poets' Pen Pal
description: Give the archive your full name (+ an optional disambiguating hint). The archivist consults only publicly-known information to try to place you specifically, then shows you a dossier — 'best guess from public record' — and asks you to confirm 'that's me' or 'not me.' The confirmation steers the tone: if identified, the follow-up questions and final handwritten letter from your epistolary twin (Keats, Woolf, Wilde, a Pony Express rider, a Cold War spy, a Renaissance alchemist, etc.) subtly echo the territory you're publicly known for. If not identified (or corrected as 'not me'), the archive gracefully writes from the name alone. The letter is styled as a yellowed handwritten page, addressed to your first name, referencing your answers.

name: Dear Drawing,
pitch: Scribble anything in a 320x320 box (no prompt, no expectations). On submit, the app reads stroke count, ink density, average stroke length, and bounding-box ratio, hashes them into a seed, and drafts a one-page handwritten-style letter addressed TO your drawing — apologizing for misreading it, asking after its family, confessing the curator's secret crush. The letter is the share artifact.
rationale: Lands in draw/letter-narrative (0 archived, 1 live — sparsest survive cell). Sidesteps the mobile-draw watchlist by making the drawing low-stakes (no prompt, no failure mode); the payoff is the letter, not the drawing. Input-restatement seam is broken: stroke-feature signals deterministically branch the letter, not just word-substitution. Amusement + parasocial tenderness arousal. LLM=light: one personalized sentence per letter (the confession line) via the AI endpoint; letter skeleton is template + seed.

name: Dear Future Me, From Right Now
pitch: Pick three chip-emojis from a 24-emoji grid that describe how today went (no typing). Pick one chip for who Future You is at the moment of opening this letter (drunk at a wedding / job interview waiting room / 4am can't sleep / on the toilet at work / waiting for test results / Christmas with the in-laws). The app generates a one-page handwritten-style letter from present-you to that future-you, referencing the three emojis as concrete events from 'today' — sealed in a stylized envelope artifact with a wax-seal stamp and date.
rationale: Lands in configure × letter-narrative (0/0 — completely untried sparse cell, the heuristic gold). All-chip input fully solves recall-from-life (recognize-not-generate from a 24-emoji palette) and wizard depth (one screen, all chips, no paragraph labor). 4 input axes (3-from-24 emojis + 1-from-~10 future-self chip) clears input-resolution coupling — >10,000 combinations into compositional output. Letter is the share artifact and is structurally hard to dismiss as a wrapper because shape requires (a) chip-to-event interpretation, (b) future-self-context tonal conditioning, (c) consistency across page — not a one-line prompt. Stance: handwritten-personal-letter aesthetic (high Form recognizability + polysemy: earnest OR ironic share both work). Arousal: tenderness + awkward vulnerability — aligned with current 'fumbled 2026, 2027 my year' meme energy. Avoids sci-fi register entirely. Caption: 'wrote myself a letter for the next time i'm drunk at a wedding'.

name: Decision Arcade
description: 10 lightning-fast binary choice scenarios (3 seconds each). Pick left or right through quick moral/preference dilemmas. Get a named archetype and axis-score card showing your decision patterns across 5 personality axes. Share your result as an emoji-grid showing choice patterns — friends immediately compare their own.

name: Direct Flash
description: Tilt your phone to compose, hit FLASH, and develop a procedural 2008-digicam paparazzi card of whatever the tilt caught — ceiling, shoes, club portrait, wall accident, DJ booth, selfie miss, drink in hand.

name: Distress Signal Triage
pitch: You are the lone comms officer on an outer-rim relay station. A garbled distress packet decodes one fragment at a time on a CRT-green console; you tap to allocate your three remaining power cells across DECODE, TRIANGULATE, or SCAN as new fragments arrive. After 90 seconds the call resolves into a stamped Incident Report — what the ship was, who survived, what you missed — that you can screenshot.
rationale: Tap-game/document-cert is a sparse but live-validated cell (2 live, 1 archived) and sci-fi mission-control fits the under-used 'instrument-credibility aesthetic' perfectly. The arousal handle is anxiety (ticking distress call, scarce resources) plus curiosity (gated reveal of who the ship was). The output is a verdict-stamped incident report — a real share artifact, not a score — and the LLM only personalizes the final report copy from your specific allocation pattern, so it passes the wrapper test (allocation history -> verdict logic). Solo-playable; same seed (date + station ID hash) gives same packet so friends can compare runs.

name: Doodle Diagnostics Bureau
description: One mechanic: doodle anything for 20 seconds on a binder-paper canvas — a heart, your old Tumblr URL in cursive, a stick-figure, whatever. The Bureau of Adolescent Doodleography stamps it as Exhibit A on a tri-folded mock 2016-era school-counselor evaluation form. Stroke geometry (loop tightness, pen-lift count, ink density, symmetry) drives a deterministic 'Adolescent Subtype' verdict ('The Notebook-Margin Romantic', 'Algebra-Class Anarchist', 'Lowercase Spiral-Bound Mystic'), a four-line behavioral diagnosis written in deadpan school-counselor voice, and a Recommended Tumblr Tag from a 2016 catalog. Yellowed mimeograph paper, MS-Comic-Sans annotations, red 'EVALUATED' stamp. Share via case-store URL that replays the recipient's doodle plus the verdict.

name: Dusk Dispatch
pitch: A single-card radio bulletin from the fictional 'Western Frequency' that re-tunes to YOUR local sun-state every time you open it. It computes your phase of day (dawn / morning / midday / golden hour / dusk / deep night) from your phone clock + IP-geolocated city, fetches one verifiable real fact (today's actual sunset minute for your city, current moon phase, what planet is highest right now via local Meeus calc), and calls the LLM to write one ~80-word noir dispatch that bakes that fact into a paragraph of weather-and-atmosphere — a different fictional region matched to your sun-state. Bottom of the card prints the verifiable anchor in monospace ('38.4°N · sunset 19:14 local · waxing crescent') so the pinning is visible. New dispatch every 6 hours, never the same twice in one day, share-button copies the dispatch as quotable text.
rationale: Time-of-day-conditional apps are an under-represented lane — the live shelf has spatial real-time apps (Sundown Line maps the global terminator, Pocket Telescope/Tonight's Sky show your sky) but nothing where the SAME app reads as a dramatically different artifact at 6am vs 8pm vs 2am. Avoids the AI-text-as-medium trap because the AI text is brief (~80 words), is a payoff for showing up at this time, and is anchored to a verifiable fact the user can confirm with their own eyes. Avoids the dashboard-many-panels mistake — single card, screenshot-able. Solo-UAT-perfect: the doing is opening it; the value is the dispatch itself. Caption-test: 'sundown 19:14 in my city and the Western Frequency is reporting' — quotable. Risk: the LLM call is the whole payload, so the prompt has to deliver a tight noir voice every time — budget hand-tuned per-sun-state prompt templates with worked examples.

name: Ecosystem Collapse Diorama
description: A tiny procedural ecosystem lives in your browser — herbivores graze, predators hunt, plants grow, and weather shifts. You watch it evolve in real time. At 5-minute milestones the system auto-labels its current state ('Precarious Balance', 'Rabbit Hegemony', 'Silent Spring') and lets you screenshot and share the labeled diorama as a named nature report. No input required — just observe and witness.

name: The Editor's Red Pen
pitch: You're handed a single short paragraph of anonymous prose — picked deterministically from a 200-piece hand-written corpus by today's date, so everyone reads the same one all day. Three tap actions on words: tap = strikethrough, long-press = '?' annotation, double-tap = blue circle (this line is the strongest). 45 seconds. At time-up, the page grades not your edits but YOU — a verdict in the voice of a 1960s New Yorker editor: 'Your editorial signature is THE STRIKETHROUGH ARSONIST: cuts 14 words, circles 0, leaves no margin notes. Recommended for: pamphlets and zines.' The marked-up page IS the share artifact (your red ink visible on the same paragraph everyone today read), and a friend hitting the share URL sees their mark-up side-by-side with yours.
rationale: Lands in a genuinely empty shape — tap-game on TEXT (not visual targets) is missing from the shelf entirely. Closest neighbours are Texting Decoder (analyzes how you type, not how you tap on supplied prose) and Decision Arcade (chips, not continuous-text interaction). The corpus-shipped-with-the-app dodges every recent input-side failure pattern at once: no recall-from-life (we supply the words — sidesteps the input-design wall), no paragraph-typing (Acquisitions Editor / Dead Poets' / Group Chat Energy Audit deprecation cluster), no draw (Suspicious Marks / Sketch Trial / Provenance Office / Doodle Diagnostics cluster), no tilt (Phantom Putt / Console Pilot / Marble Notary cluster), no sci-fi register (Captain's Log / Distress Signal / Generation Ship / Larp Bot cluster), no AI-image-headline. The verdict branches on real behavioural signal across three independent axes (cut count, circle count, annotation count) — passes the input-restatement-seam test because two users with the same edit-counts but different distributions get different verdicts. Caption: 'turns out I'm a strikethrough arsonist with zero margin notes.' Verdict-desirability: every editor archetype is a flex (the surgical cutter, the gentle praiser, the chaotic annotator). Cultural fit: 'Academic Weapon' niche-trend plus the anti-AI-slop authenticity wave makes 'I am the editor of human writing' a live job-to-be-done. Risk: the 200-paragraph corpus has to be genuinely good (the Bureau of the Current Minute precedent shows 10,080 lines is tractable, so 200 is well within budget). Differentiates cleanly from Bureau of the Current Minute (passive read) and Decision Arcade (binary chips).

name: Elevator Bingo
description: A 60-second pixel-art elevator ride plays out — passengers board at each floor drawn from a deterministic daily seed of 12 archetypes (the Phone-Sigh-er, the Yoga-Pants Lurker, the Aggressive Nodder, the Phantom Floor-Presser, the Coffee-Sloshing CEO, the Door-Hold Hero, the Mirror-Checker, the Suitcase Wrangler, the Earbud Hermit, the Floor-Button Apologist, the Smelly Lunch, the Whisperer-on-Phone). Tap each passenger as you ID their archetype from a 12-tile bingo card before the doors close on floor 30. Final score is rendered as a stamped 'Field Notes from Floor 30' card with your named verdict ('Elevator Sociologist, Class III'), today's hardest-catch (whichever archetype the most users missed), and a hand-drawn pixel map of who you correctly tagged. Same ride for everyone today. Tomorrow's ride is different.

name: Exquisite Corpse
description: A pass-and-play surreal creature-drawing game for two people on one phone. Player 1 draws the top half of a made-up creature on a split canvas; the phone hides what they drew, passes to Player 2, who draws the bottom half blind. The reveal stitches the halves into one creature and names it with a deterministic LLM call based on extracted geometric features (stroke count, angularity, symmetry, bounding boxes). Named verdicts like The Gilded Snarler appear with a field-guide blurb in the voice of a Victorian naturalist. Share = URL fragment encoding both strokesets; recipient lands on the full creature replay and can start their own round.

name: Draw Your Signature, Get Your Forgery Report
description: One primary action: sign your name on a canvas with your finger or mouse — exactly like signing a package. The Handwriting Bureau issues a deadpan forensic examiner's report analyzing geometric features of the actual strokes (loop tightness, slant variance, pen-speed spikes, letter-size ratio, avg pen-lift duration, path length, stroke count, bounding-box aspect). Output is a tri-folded mock FBI Questioned Documents lab report with a traced Exhibit A of your signature, an 8-field analytics panel, a three-line forgery verdict, a named signatory archetype (The Confident Embezzler, The Trembling Diplomat, etc.), and a red CLASSIFIED stamp. Share fragment encodes stroke data via case-store so recipients see your exact signature replay then sign their own.

name: Fortune Vending
description: A pixel-art vending machine dispenses today's fortune. Drop a coin, mash the big red button, watch a can clunk down the chute with a satisfying thud, then peel the tab to reveal one hand-stamped line — specific, dated, same for everyone today. Three cans max per day so the ritual stays scarce.

name: Generation Ship Roster
pitch: Six dials: cohort size, decades adrift, dominant trade, founding myth, recent loss, the rule no one follows. Slide them and watch a 200-person generation-ship roster regenerate live — names, ages, jobs, who's pregnant, who's in stasis, who just died — printed on green-bar dot-matrix paper as a scrolling crew manifest. Reads like real census output. Same dial settings = same roster.
rationale: configure/document-cert is sparse (1 archived, 0 live) and explicitly avoids the heavy-LLM trap flagged in ai-pitfalls (no LLM at runtime — the roster is generated procedurally from name banks + simple demographic rules, so the dials -> output causality is deterministic and visible). Mock-bureaucratic + monospace dot-matrix lands squarely in the validated 'instrument-credibility' aesthetic. Real causality (every dial visibly shifts the manifest), no image-gen wrapper risk, no daily-anchor problem (the dials ARE the input). Share artifact is the long printout — works as a Reddit thumbnail. Solo-UAT-able and reproducible via URL fragment.

name: Ghost Receipt
description: Tap a curling thermal-paper receipt and absurd line items materialize one by one — wrong taxis, sentences you never finished, apologies you owed yourself. Twelve taps prints your final NIGHT OUT total, a screenshottable mock-bureaucratic ledger of a night that got away from you.

name: Gravity Doodle
description: A falling-sand sandbox where users invent their own elements. Six built-in materials (wall, sand, water, oil, fire, plant) interact via composable physics rules; tap 'invent element' to generate a new one via AI — name it + describe its vibe and the LLM returns a structured spec (kind, density, colors, reactions with existing elements) that joins the palette for the session. Paint, pour, watch cascading reactions.

name: Group Chat Energy Audit
description: Paste 5–10 messages you've sent in your group chat (or enter your name + pick 4–6 behavioral chips). The app produces a formal-looking OSHA-style inspection report with a verdict role ('Certified Chaos Engineer,' 'The Silent Auditor,' 'Designated Vibe Supervisor'), a bulleted list of citations quoting your own messages back, a hazard rating, and a stamp. Downloadable PNG with a 'get your own audit' CTA for recipients.

name: The Group Chat Eulogy
pitch: Type ONE sentence: the moment a group chat you're in started dying ('when Sarah got engaged', 'when Marco moved to Berlin', 'when we all turned 28'). Pick a chip for which member of the chat you were (the planner / the lurker / the meme account / the one who left first). The app generates a 3-paragraph eulogy in the voice of a dignified funeral celebrant for that specific group chat, closing with a 'cause of death' verdict — rendered as a black-bordered funeral program with a date range, a 'beloved by [chip-derived list of fictional members]' line, and a parting quote.
rationale: Single sentence + one chip — no recall-from-life cost, no actual chat data needed (sidesteps the messaging-platform wall from input-design.md). Premise is universally relatable and currently culturally salient (post-pandemic group-chat decay is recurring 2026 discourse, lining up with the 'fumbled 2026' meme energy from web-search). Funeral-program Form is highly meme-shaped (recognizable across users); stance is mock-sacred (BVT canonical pattern: sacred framing on profane content, like the spite calculators). Arousal: amusement + relatable melancholy (both high-arousal, share-driving). Wrapper test passes via multi-section structure (eulogy paragraphs + cause-of-death verdict + program layout chrome). Verdict-desirability passes — every cause of death is shareable ('cause of death: mass adulthood'). User-as-chip identifier ('which member were you') gives identity-affirmation alongside the document, doubling the share motive. Caption: 'rip the group chat 2018-2024'.

name: Grow My Civilization
description: Watch a tiny pixel civilization start from a single campfire and either bloom into an empire or collapse into rubble — all without touching anything. The trajectory is seeded by today's date, so everyone witnesses the same fate unfold. At the collapse or triumph moment (roughly 90 seconds), the app delivers a named 'Civilization Verdict' — 'The Bronze Age Cowards', 'The Uranium Gourmands', 'The Paperclip Maximalists' — with a one-sentence historian's epitaph styled as a museum plaque. Share button produces a URL fragment that replays the same run.

name: Hard Launch My Mundane
description: Type 4 small things you've been weirdly devoted to this week — the snack, the show, the playlist, the new hyperfixation — and the app produces a 4-card swipeable polaroid 'soft launch' carousel introducing each one as your new romantic partner, in flirty soft-launch-IG caption voice. The carousel layout IS the meme template; instantly recognizable as 'a Hard Launch post' regardless of which user made it. Shareable via URL fragment for short payloads or case-store short-id for longer ones; recipient lands on the same carousel hydrated from the link.

name: Heirloom Key-Cutter
description: A pixel-art locksmith's bench. Six brass dials carve a custom key tooth-by-tooth; the live-readout panel shows the cutting pattern updating in real time. Click 'Test the key' and your single profile is run against today's daily-seeded catalog of 30 fictional historic locks. Each opened lock reveals its name + one-line provenance fact. Reveal is a stamped Locksmith's Provenance Card with brass corner-seals, downloadable as PNG, plus a permalink that replays the same key + same daily catalog.

name: Heist Plotter
description: A mock after-action heist generator. The screen shows a tiny pixel-art floor plan (vault / penthouse / museum / chocolate factory). The user clicks 5 numbered waypoints in sequence to plot the route — entry, distraction, target, switch-back, exfil. The path itself is the input. On submit, the Bureau of Notable Capers issues a tri-folded after-action poster: a named alias ("Maestro of the Rear Stairwell", "The Lobby Whisperer"), a route map of the user's exact path as Exhibit A, a loot tally derived from path geometry (zigzag length, time near guards, doors crossed), three deadpan named accomplices, and a CASE: CLOSED stamp with verdict ("Clean", "Botched", "Legendary").

name: Home Screen Confessions
description: Type the 5 apps you open most from your phone's home screen; the site reads them as a cultural-generational fingerprint and hands you a named verdict ('The Unemployable Mystic', 'The Dopamine Accountant') rendered on a stylized fake home screen where those 5 apps are pinned around a brass name plate. Uses the LLM decoder shape to interpret the specific combination (not a lookup). One share image, one caption, one clear premise.

name: How 2016 Are You?
description: A nostalgia calculator that scores how deeply you lived the 2016 internet era. Answer 8 questions about your Vine habits, Tumblr usage, Snapchat streaks, and meme fluency. Get a % score plus a named archetype — 'Peak Tumblr Kid', 'Vine Energizer', 'The Mannequin Challenger', etc.

name: Hummingbird Daily
pitch: Once per day, the app shows a single circle and plays a target pitch (440Hz on day 1, varies daily by date seed). You hold the circle and hum into your phone — the mic samples your pitch, locks the moment you stop, and renders your absolute deviation in cents from the target. Live histogram shows where every other hummer landed today. Verdict: 'PERFECT (within 5 cents)', 'PRETTY GOOD', 'TONE-DEAF DARLING'. Three attempts, best one counts.
rationale: Voice input is completely absent from the shelf — the closest neighbor is Two Octaves (tap-when-it-rises octave-judge), which uses ears but not voice; nothing else asks for the mic. Inherits the live-histogram social-proof model that Closer to 1.000 (published) proved viable, but with a fresh mechanic. Solo-UAT: one user, one phone, one mic. Mobile-native — phone mic is high-quality and Web Audio API needs no key. Caption test passes: 'I hummed today's note within 4 cents, my ancestors were songbirds.' Risk: mic permission prompt may scare users; mitigation is a clear pre-prompt screen ('we don't record audio — we only measure pitch and discard') and a fallback 'tap when you think the tone has matched yours' mode for permission-denied. Different from Two Octaves: that measures listening; this measures producing. Fills the audio-result gap and the daily-comparable-score gap simultaneously.

name: Kite String Physics
description: A single-line kite you fly on touch/mouse drag — the cursor is the reel, the wind is a live vector field you can see as faint streamlines. Let out line, reel in, sweep across the sky. Procedural wind gusts push the kite in legible ways; a small bird flocks around you; a cloud occasionally drifts through. The only goal is staying aloft longer and doing loops. Each loop/figure-eight/nosedive-recovery earns a named 'trick' stamp ('double cobra', 'faint heart'). After ~60s a pocket 'flight log' card gets stamped with your route (silhouette of the actual path you flew) + the tricks you landed + day's wind label ('apr 19: gusty southerly'). Share = URL-fragment encoding of the seed + path, recipient sees your exact flight replay then takes their own.

name: Koi Coin Rally
description: A 60-second kawaii pixel-art race where you ride a chibi koi fish surfing down a winding river race-track. Tilt left/right with arrow keys (desktop) or tap left/right halves of the screen (mobile) to weave between lily pads, dodge cranky frogs, and scoop up gold coins. Three lanes, a single continuous river, a finish-line gate. The coin total at the finish converts deterministically into a named pilot license — 'Koi Cadet Sumiko (47 coins)', 'Reckless Sushi Express (88 coins)', 'Lord Mochi of the Coursed Stream (120+)'. Daily seeded race-track means everyone gets the same course today; share card is your fish portrait + license title + coin emoji-grid for the run.

name: Larp Bot
pitch: You write one sentence trying to sound as much like AI as possible (topic chip prompts the angle: 'leadership advice', 'wellness tip', 'startup pitch', 'breakup text'). The app scores your line on a deterministic AI-likeness rubric — em-dash count, hedge-density, vague intensifiers ('truly', 'meaningful', 'authentic'), tricolon rhythm, sentence-length variance, the dead-giveaway closer ('not just X, but Y'). You get a 0–100 'Synth Score' and a verdict: Confirmed Synth / Suspicious Carbon / Authentically Human / Try Harder. Replay until you crack 95 — the app stamps your highest-scoring line as a 'Certified AI Slop' specimen card.
rationale: Rides the 'Your AI Slop Bores Me' viral moment but inverts the shape — instead of the user judging AI text, the user performs as AI and gets graded. There is no AI in the loop, which dodges the wrapper-shape critique entirely — it's a deterministic text-feature classifier. Solo-UAT-perfect: replay-driven, score-game, no strangers. Caption-test passes immediately ('I scored 97% AI with one sentence'). Verdict-desirability passes — every bucket is flex-worthy. Differentiates from anything on the shelf — closest neighbors are Texting Decoder and FOBO Simulator; Larp Bot is the user trying to become the AI, an active competitive performance not a passive judgment. Risk: rubric must be tight enough that scores feel earned — needs hand-tuned weights on a small training corpus of real LLM output.

name: The Library of Returned Books
description: A pixel-art library cart with 12 weirdly-specific spine titles. Pick any 4 books and the librarian hands you the typewritten letter the previous patron left tucked inside — a melancholy first-person note from a fictional stranger on a specific date in the past, explaining why those four books, in that combination, on that week. Risograph-on-yellowed-cardstock with a sleeping pixel cat. Share-link replays the same 4-book pick and the same letter via case-store.

name: Lowercase Court
description: Read six anonymous texts and deliver a verdict (guilty / not guilty / mistrial) with a punishment chip. After 6 judgments, the app reveals your named judicial archetype on a mock court docket with your six rulings quoted back. Share via URL fragment so friends get the same six cases.

name: Marble Notary
pitch: Tilt your phone like a spirit-level to roll a single marble through a notary office's stamp pads. Each pad you cross stamps your Officially Notarized Personality (witnessed-by, attested-on, jurisdiction-of). Three short courses (~25s each). Pose-zero capture on Start; on-screen marble is the one-step metaphor. Generated certificate at the end with pad-order baked in.
rationale: Tilt-rotate is surviving (0 archived) and document-cert layer makes the artifact share-card-ready. Honors device-orientation-controls: marble is a direct one-step metaphor, mandatory pose-zero, asymmetric pad layout rewards directional commitment, <60s session before drift. Bureaucratic-deadpan frame (amusement arousal) lifts the user — the office is the absurdity. Drag-fallback works on desktop. Document-cert shape clears the bare-archetype watchlist.

name: Melody Guesser
description: A daily challenge puzzle: six audio clips of a well-known melody play in increasing length (0.5s, 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s). The player guesses the song title after each clip — fewest clues needed wins. One puzzle per day, seeded by date. Share your streak and guess count: 'Got today's Melody Guesser in 2 clues! Day 7 streak'. Tones generated with Web Audio API using a note-sequence database — no external API key needed.

name: Ministry of Minor Regrets
description: A bureaucratic-audit calculator. Submit six mundane daily numbers; receive an itemized audit of regrets stamped by the Ministry.

name: Minor Saint of [Your Devotion]
description: Finger-trace a halo on a blank card and type one mundane thing you are weirdly devoted to. The Order issues a deterministic minor-saint verdict — Saint Mira, Patron of Half-Watched Documentaries — and renders your traced halo onto a risograph prayer card with the saint's name, patronage, and a four-line deadpan prayer. The halo geometry actually conditions the saint name (small spiky halo → Saint of the Stubborn; wide gentle halo → Saint of the Slow). Riso-print zine aesthetic — limited palette, ink-bleed, off-register print. Share via case-store URL that replays the exact halo + saint.

name: Name to Galaxy
description: Type any name (or word) and watch the browser instantly render a unique procedural galaxy for it: star density, nebula color clouds, and a central object (star cluster or black hole silhouette) are all seeded from the name's character hash. The galaxy is named 'The [Name] Nebula' and a one-line flavor fact is pulled from NumbersAPI using the character count as the number seed. A 'Download my galaxy' button exports the full-resolution canvas as a shareable image. Entirely client-side, works on mobile.

name: Niche Hall of Fame
description: Type the weirdly specific thing you are unreasonably passionate about (ranking gas station coffee, collecting novelty soap, sorting pens by mood). The app inducts you with a pompous certificate: your official title (The Commissioner of Minor Soap), era of reign, patron saint, and a 2-sentence induction speech from the Hall's emcee. Plus 'today's fellow inductee' - a seeded daily rival everyone gets. Share as a URL-fragment certificate.

name: One-Phone Charades Duel
pitch: Pass-and-play head-to-head on a single phone. Player A taps a tile from today's seeded deck of 20 absurdly specific things ('the feeling of finding a 20 in last winter's coat'). The phone hides the screen; Player B has 30 seconds to guess by asking yes/no questions while Player A tilts the phone forward (yes) or back (no). Phone times the rounds and counts correct. Five rounds each, both players use the same deck (deterministic by date), so two friends can play independently and compare scores via a share URL.
rationale: Multiplayer head-to-head is one of the most underexplored shapes on the shelf — only Reflex Duel II and Cartograph Duel exist, and both are reflex/drawing-based. A pure-cognitive duel is missing entirely. Pass-and-play means it works in person AND solo-UAT-able (you pass the phone between your own hands to verify). The daily-deck-seed means two friends in different cities can play asynchronously and compare results — that's the 'connection' job from the cultural-cartography taxonomy, which the shelf barely touches. The tilt-as-answer is a sensor-native mechanic that earns the device-orientation use (one-step monotonic metaphor, satisfies the device-orientation-controls rules). Caption: 'My sister and I got 4/5 on today's One-Phone deck.' Risk: pass-and-play presupposes two friends in a room together — daily-seeded comparison mode is the solo escape hatch.

name: One-Stroke Heist
description: A daily canvas-game puzzle with a heist theme. Each day the vault layout is different: 6–10 scattered gems (plus a few trap pixels) sit on a dark museum floor. The player has exactly ONE continuous finger/mouse stroke — lifting or crossing their own path ends the run. Goal: sweep through as many gems as possible without touching a trap. Score = gems cleared out of total, plus a stroke-efficiency indicator. Seeded by date so everyone attempts the same layout; result screen produces a compact emoji-grid share plus a replay-ready permalink. Single player, works on desktop + mobile, fully client-side.

name: Outfit Archetypes
description: Take a photo of your outfit today. The app analyzes color blocking, silhouette, and vibe to assign you a named fashion archetype ('The Maximalist Curator', 'Stealth Luxury Understater', 'Chaotic Thrift Spirit'). Result shows your archetype badge + a one-sentence style diagnosis that feels eerily accurate. Shareable card has your archetype name. Designed to feel like a personal style oracle, not a judgment.

name: Particle Life
description: A Particle Life simulation in the browser: hundreds of coloured particles follow simple attraction/repulsion rules that produce emergent flocking, clustering, and cell-like behaviour. Users can tweak the force matrix sliders in real time and watch the world reorganise. One 'Screenshot my universe' button exports a named snapshot (seeded from the current rule set) for sharing.

name: Personal Emblem Forge
description: Enter your name and pick 3 personality traits (e.g., 'ambitious', 'curious', 'loyal'). The app procedurally generates a unique heraldic-style personal emblem on canvas — a shield shape, symbolic animal (seeded from name hash), pattern fills, accent colors, and a generated motto. Same inputs always produce the same emblem. Rendered in a bold medieval-woodcut aesthetic (black lines, limited rich palette). A 'Download my emblem' button exports the canvas as a shareable image. Entirely client-side, works on mobile.

name: Petty Small Claims
description: Describe an everyday grievance and pick from human-language aggravating factors and petty damages — no numbers anywhere. The clerk handles all math behind the scenes and reveals the awarded amount only at the end as a dramatic typewritten judgment with three LLM findings, a flattering verdict, and a serve-the-defendant share flow.

name: Phantom Putt
pitch: A daily mini-golf hole drawn in pen on graph paper. Tilt your phone to roll the ball, count strokes, share a Wordle-style stroke grid. Same hole for everyone today.
rationale: Lands in the sparse tilt-rotate row alongside the active direct-flash and antipode winners — device-orientation substrate is currently performing. Daily-shared course with emoji-grid stroke share rides the observe×daily-reveal hot streak (Tonight's Sky, Tide Diviner, Pocket Telescope) but in a different mechanic cell. Hand-drawn graph-paper aesthetic deliberately fights AI-default polish (anti-viral cluster per Deza & Parikh). Caption test passes: 'par 4, I got 11.'
description: A daily mini-golf hole drawn in pen on graph paper. Tilt your phone to roll the ball, count strokes, share a Wordle-style stroke grid. Same hole for everyone today.

name: The Pilgrim's Week
pitch: Day 1: a single illustrated chamber appears with one binary choice — take the gold key, take the silver key, or take neither. That's the entire interaction. The page stamps a postcard: 'CHOICE RECORDED. NEXT CHAMBER OPENS TOMORROW.' Your URL preserves your seven-choice progress; you can share or bookmark. Day 2 (a fresh visit, real next calendar day): a different chamber with a different binary, hand-curated per day-of-week (the locked door / the unlocked one; the path with bells / the path with no sound). Each day's choice is small and visceral. By Day 7, the cumulative path through the seven binaries deterministically composes a Pilgrim's Page — the Order of the Quiet Step, the Order of the Hurried Hand, the Order of Two Returns — with a one-paragraph history of your specific path written in the voice of a medieval scribe. Each day's postcard is shareable, AND the final pilgrim badge is the climactic share artifact.
rationale: Multi-day continuity is genuinely missing from the portfolio — every existing app is single-session or daily-restart. Even Bureau of the Current Minute and Fortune Vending pin to a single moment, not to a path through time. Lands in a brand-new shape: longitudinal-input × ceremonial-document. Mechanically dramatically simpler than any wizard-stack app that recently failed: each day is one binary tap (no paragraph-typing, no draw, no tilt, no recall-from-life). The wizard-stack failure mode (Dead Poets, Cryptid 2.0, Acquisitions Editor) is structurally inverted — instead of forcing all input in one session, the input is distributed across seven 30-second returns, so daily friction stays sub-30-seconds even though total session-equivalent input is rich. Cultural fit: the cozy/slow-living and tiny-daily-ritual trends (Tiny Career Moments) reward apps that ask for almost nothing daily. Verdict-desirability: every Pilgrim Order is a flex with a flavor (the Quiet Step, the Hurried Hand, the Two Returns, the Echo Listener). Risk: the bet is multi-day retention — if day-2 return is below ~20% the climax never lands for most users. Two mitigations: (1) every day's individual postcard is caption-worthy on its own ('CHAMBER 1 RECORDED: I took the gold key. Six to go.'), so the social loop fires from day 1, not just from day 7; (2) URL preserves all state so a friend can share the day-7 page directly and a recipient can do all seven on the same day if they want, just in private (the seven calendar days is the canonical mode, the 'binge in one sitting' is a fallback). Differentiates from every existing daily-anchor app (which is one-and-done) and from Closer to 1.000 (single-session percentile).

name: Pipe Connect
description: A daily spatial puzzle: a grid of cells with colored endpoints — draw paths to connect matching pairs without crossing. One puzzle per day, freshly generated by date seed. After solving, share your completion time and a compact emoji-grid of your solution path as a spoiler-free result. Streak counter keeps players coming back daily.

name: Pocket Telescope
description: Geolocate (or pick a city) and the app computes which of tonight's visible celestial objects (Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, ISS pass, current bright comet, today's strongest meteor radiant) is highest in your sky right now via pure-client ephemeris (Meeus). The hero panel is a single big circular eyepiece view of that object. Twelve toggleable lenses each render the same object in the annotated sketch style of a different historical astronomer/observatory: Galileo's quill, Cassini's wash, Herschel's hatch, Lyot's coronagraph plate, Voyager grayscale, JWST false-color IR, etc. Each toggle is a fresh screenshot-able artifact labeled with units, dates, and a one-line code-comment header ("// after Galileo, 1610-01-07"). Permalink encodes location + selected lens so the page is the share. Instrument-credibility aesthetic: black background, monospace pills, code-comment subheads, single warm accent.

name: The Probate of an Imaginary Stranger
description: A pixel-art top-down view of a deceased eccentric's one-bedroom apartment with 20 objects scattered across rooms (tin of mints, half-finished crossword, velvet sock, cassette labeled 'DO NOT', brass owl, stack of romance novels, etc.). User taps 7 items to choose their probate inventory. The Office of the Public Trustee issues a tri-folded official Probate Inventory document: lot-numbered list of chosen items with absurd appraisal lines, a named 'Most Probable Identity' verdict for the deceased pulled from a 24-archetype catalog conditioned on the specific item combination, a 4-line clerk's note quoting picks back, ESTATE: SETTLED stamp. Mock-bureaucratic typewriter / manilla-folder aesthetic. URL-fragment share replays same picks deterministically.

name: Proof of Human Audit
pitch: Type one paragraph on any topic (what you ate today, why you hate your job, defense of pineapple pizza). The app silently records typing rhythm: keystroke intervals, backspace count, ALL-CAPS ratio, em-dash usage, double-space-after-period, words-per-minute consistency, punctuation chaos. It then issues an officially stamped 'Proof of Human Score' certificate — typewritten findings ('SUBJECT BACKSPACED 14 TIMES — DECISIVELY HUMAN', 'EM-DASH ABUSE INDEX: GENERATION ZED'), a percentage score, and a passport-style stamp ('VERIFIED HUMAN' / 'AI-ADJACENT' / 'TURING DROPOUT'). The stamped doc IS the share artifact, not a verdict line.
rationale: Rides the May 2026 'Proof of Human' cultural moment (Mosseri Instagram pivot toward unproduced/raw content, Backslash 'Proof of Human' report, Gartner 50% anti-AI-ad finding) — timely without being trend-chasing because the underlying mechanic (typing-behavior fingerprint) is an honest measurement, not a vibe. The shelf has many bureaucratic-cert apps (Petty Small Claims, Suspicious Marks, FOBO Sim) but none audit the user's *literal keystrokes* — that's the differentiator: the input IS the typing itself, not just the words. Avoids the bare-archetype-text watchlist (N=2) by shipping a document-cert artifact form, which the watchlist hypothesis suggests is the load-bearing part. Self-deprecating + flattering paths are both available depending on findings, satisfying the polysemy rule from shareability-design. Caption: 'apparently I'm 87% human, the missing 13% is em-dashes'. Risk: typing-rhythm data is collected silently — needs a clear pre-screen disclosure ('we measure how you type, not what you type'). Differs from the receipt/cert cluster because the audit subject is *behavioral*, not declarative.

name: Provenance Office
description: Draw any object on a yellowed-paper canvas. Live deterministic appraisal (stroke count, ink density, aspect ratio, presumed era, estimated rarity, craftsmanship score) updates as you draw. On submit, a fictional curator at the Northbrook Civic Museum writes a single-page acquisition letter pleading the board to buy the artifact for an absurd sum, with the drawing pasted in as a sepia archive thumbnail (Fig. 1).

name: Ransom Note Forge
description: A text-to-ransom-note generator. Type any short message and get it back as a classic cut-out-letters ransom note — each character rendered as a different magazine/newspaper clipping with varied fonts, paper textures, and rotations. Re-roll to reshuffle, and save the result as a PNG.

name: Reaction Diffusion Studio
description: A Gray-Scott reaction diffusion simulator running on HTML Canvas. Click or drag to seed chemical patterns anywhere on the canvas — watch Turing-style spots, stripes, and labyrinthine organism-like textures emerge in real time. Four preset modes (spots, coral, fingerprints, maze) plus three tunable sliders (feed rate, kill rate, diffusion ratio). A 'Save my organism' button exports the canvas as a full-resolution shareable image. No win state — pure mesmerizing emergent biology.

name: Reality TV Reaction Engine
description: Tap a reaction-tier chip ten times as 10 short pixel-art mundane moments scroll by — POLITE GASP / DRAMATIC PAUSE / CONFESSIONAL BOOTH / VILLAIN EDIT. Your ten reactions deterministically score four axes (drama-density, pettiness-velocity, confessional-honesty, villain-arc) and produce a named Reality-TV-Casting verdict on a casting-call clipboard with a 2x5 chip-stamped thumbnail grid and a deadpan casting-director quote.

name: Red-String Theory
description: Type 5 totally mundane things about your week and get a paranoid 1970s corkboard conspiracy theory connecting them — complete with typewritten index cards, red strings with cryptic labels, a named grand-unified theory title, a CLASSIFIED stamp, and a threat-level banner. Shareable via URL fragment that replays the exact same board.

name: Reflex Duel
description: Two players join via a room code. A countdown runs, then a colored circle flashes at a random screen position — first player to tap or click it wins the round. Best of 7 rounds. Reaction time is displayed after each round, and sub-200ms earns a 'Superhuman Reflex' badge. The winner shares a challenge card: 'I beat my friend 4-3 with a best reaction of 187ms — can you dethrone me?' Sessions end in under 3 minutes.

name: Reflex Duel II
description: Two players join by room code. A yellow circle flashes at a random spot — first to tap it wins. Best-of-7 with server-adjudicated verdicts (no more double-winner bug from V1). Tap before the circle appears and it's an instant 'TOO SOON' false start. Sub-200ms reactions earn a Superhuman Reflex badge. Winner shares a challenge card.

name: Rhythm Tap
description: A canvas-based rhythm game where colored note tiles fall from the top of the screen in sync with a procedurally generated beat (Web Audio API). Tap or click each tile as it hits the target zone — perfect hits score more, misses break your combo. Songs increase in BPM as the score grows. At game over, players see their accuracy percentage, longest combo, and a grade (S/A/B/C).

name: Sand Mandala Machine
description: A configure-to-reveal creative artifact: the user dials a set of abstract sliders (chaos level, color temperature, symmetry axis, grain density) — no drawing required — and watches a procedural sand mandala slowly render itself in real time. When it settles, they get a named mandala archetype ("The Crumbling Order," "The Fever Dream Compass") plus a downloadable share card showing the finished pattern and the sliders that made it. Seeded — same settings always produce the same mandala.

name: Sentence in B Minor
pitch: Type any sentence (your ex's name, your email signature, a Slack message that ruined your day). The app deterministically maps it to a 12-second piano loop in B minor — characters become notes by ASCII mod 12, spaces become rests, punctuation triggers percussion hits, sentence length sets tempo. The result plays automatically with a hand-drawn cassette-label visual showing the sentence as ink-spattered title. Share button copies a URL whose fragment encodes your sentence; recipients open it and hear the exact same loop with no replay. Built on Tone.js (CDN-pinned, no key needed).
rationale: Audio-as-result-artifact is genuinely absent from the shelf — Two Octaves and the archived Melody Guesser are the only sound-touching apps and neither produces a shareable musical artifact tied to user input. The deterministic-replay-via-URL pattern is exactly what the shareable-state-urls concept page recommends for create-an-artifact apps. No LLM dependence (avoids ChatGPT-wrapper complaint). Mobile-native autoplay-on-button-press fits the audio-constraints rules (procedural, no copyrighted audio). Caption: 'this is what my work email signature sounds like in B minor'. Risk: 12-second listen is a higher commitment than a screenshot — mitigation is the cassette-label visual that's screenshot-shareable on its own and primes the recipient to actually press play. Differs from everything on the shelf because the payoff is sound, not a doc/cert/quiz/score.

name: The Autopsy of My Last Situationship
description: User enters a few details about a dead relationship (duration, the vibe, how it ended) and receives an official mock Coroner's Report: clinical cause of death, toxicology screen (substances detected: unread messages, vague future plans, breadcrumbs), time of death, and a stamped verdict. Styled as a medical examiner's form with rubber stamps and clinical jargon. Single-page generator with shareable result.

name: Sketch Trial
description: Draw the criminal you imagine when given a single absurd crime description ("stole the last bagel," "replied-all to a corporate-wide email at 11:47pm," "returned a romance novel in worse condition"). Stroke geometry — face shape, eye spacing, jaw set, eyebrow severity — is measured and run against a 30-suspect-archetype catalog. The Bureau of Forensic Sketch Evaluation issues a wanted-poster verdict naming your suspect ("The Lateral Brunch Bandit, age 34, last seen wearing performative running shoes"), with quoted geometric exhibits and your actual sketch reproduced as Exhibit A. Risograph wanted-poster aesthetic.

name: Slime Mold Simulator
description: Physarum polycephalum simulation where users place food sources on a dark canvas and watch a living network of slime mold tendrils grow, branch, and optimize paths between food. Users can add, remove, or drag food sources to reshape the network in real time. Visually mesmerizing — the network self-organizes into minimal spanning trees. A 'Save my organism' button exports the canvas as a shareable image.

name: Snowglobe Photographer
description: Shake or tilt your phone to rearrange the objects falling inside a physics-simulated snowglobe until they match today's silhouette target (a rabbit, a heart, a skull, etc.). Tap to take the photo when the overlap is highest. Score = peak percentage pixel match. Daily seeded scene, local best, emoji-grid share.

name: Specimen Drift
description: An ambient deep-sea aquarium where 30 procedurally-illustrated abyssal creatures drift across a black canvas. Tap any creature to freeze it as a Specimen Card — an engraved-Victorian field plate with a deterministic latin binomial seeded from its behavior fingerprint, a four-line naturalist's note, and a dated catalog number. Curate a 6-card expedition log; the log itself is the share artifact, riso-printed sepia, exported as a single PNG. Every visit reseeds the swarm.

name: Split the Bill With Spite
description: Enter 3-6 people's names and paste one line per person describing what they did at dinner (e.g. 'Ben ordered the lobster,' 'Sarah forgot her wallet again,' 'Kai talked about crypto for 40 minutes'). The app returns an itemized bill-split receipt with a spite-adjusted dollar amount per person plus a named verdict per person ('The Unpaid Narrator,' 'The Calendar Saboteur,' 'The Lobster Heiress'). Rendered as a modern Venmo/Splitwise-style receipt graphic with a punchy sans-serif display face. Deterministic on input; shareable via URL fragment that replays the same receipt.

name: Static Shock Tuner
description: Drag across a CRT-style static field to 'tune' a hidden daily frequency. A sine-wave needle snaps toward the carrier as you approach; locking onto it for 1.5 seconds reveals today's numbers-station broadcast — a short, absurd, deterministic message. Same broadcast for everyone that day, but your path to it is yours.

name: Stop The Line
description: A single-tap risograph reflex toy. Ten daily-seeded rounds of a scrolling newspaper press — stop the line when your target word enters the red guillotine, and your average pixel deviation earns you a Printer Title on a shareable front-page clipping.

name: Stowaway Manifest
description: The user picks one of 8 absurd pixel-art passenger archetypes (The Diplomat's Cat, The Carpetbagger, The Stowaway Monk, The Calendar Bandit, etc.) to slip aboard today's departing zeppelin, then watches a 60-second seeded voyage play out — storms, customs checks, a kraken, a rival airship. At landing, the Customs House issues an official tri-folded Daily Manifest: the chosen passenger's stamped fate at port, three named customs inspectors' verdicts ('Spiritually Inadmissible Cargo', 'Released Pending Vibes'), a hand-drawn route map of what happened, and a featured cargo audit. Same passenger × same date = same voyage. Different passenger picks visibly change the journey. Mock-bureaucratic typewriter aesthetic, faded customs stamps, period maritime ink. Share is the manifest PNG plus a URL fragment that replays the same voyage.

name: Department of Suspicious Marks
description: Doodle one mark on a canvas. The Department of Suspicious Marks issues a sworn typewriter affidavit identifying your drawing as evidence in a fictional case — geometric measurements (closure index, jaggedness, asymmetry, coverage density) are quoted into the document body, the mark is classified into one of ten deterministic mock-bureaucratic case types (Looping Confessional, Spiked Affirmation, Striated Industrial, Vertical Vow, etc.), and the actual drawing is reproduced inside the seal as Exhibit A. Live geometric readouts update while drawing so users can predict their classification before filing.

name: Tab Autopsy
description: Enter the titles of six open browser tabs and receive a dead-pan coroner's autopsy report — a named archetype from a 24-strong catalog (or a freshly invented 25th), plus a time-of-death micro-roast for each tab, rendered as a manila-clipboard case file. Share links encode the six tabs in the URL fragment so the same autopsy reproduces deterministically for anyone who opens the link.

name: Tank Verdict
description: A nano-aquarium personality oracle. The tank is already running when you land — six tiny pixel fish darting through driftwood and a slow algae bloom on a dark glass canvas. You don't pet them, you don't feed them: you just watch for 60 seconds while a hidden ethologist scores six visible behaviors (shoaling tightness, surface-vs-bottom dwelling, glass-pacing, hierarchy fights, hide-out time, food-chase ferocity). At the end the tank is named and the dominant fish is crowned with a deadpan biotope-society plaque: 'The Glass-Pacing Dynasty', 'A Quiet Zen Pool', 'The Shrimp Mafia'. Each session reseeds (hash of timestamp + a 'shake the tank' button to reseed manually) so reruns visibly behave differently. Share is a screenshot of the labeled tank-as-portrait with the verdict caption — no dialog, the tab IS the share. Aquascape aesthetic: minimalist black-water biotope, off-register risograph greens, single warm light from above.

name: Tap to Wake the Cat
pitch: An ASCII-art cat is asleep at the center of the screen, snoring with an irregular rhythm. Tap exactly when you think you can wake it without scaring it — you have to feel the gaps in its breath. You get 5 taps in 30 seconds. Based on tap timing precision and pattern, the cat reacts (purrs / bolts / glares / stretches / forgives you). After your 5 taps, you get a typewritten 'Note From the Cat' addressed to you — what it thought of you, in its specific judgmental voice.
rationale: Lands in tap-game × letter-narrative (1 archived/0 live — sparse with only one prior data point, not a pattern). Cats are the single most virality-correlated subject per Deza & Parikh (animals attribute is one of the strongest image-virality predictors — disproportionately robust). 30-second mobile session, autotelic micro-loop (each tap has feedback within 100ms via snore-wave visual + cat micro-reaction). Clear competence arc within session (tap 1 calibrates, taps 4-5 have stakes), one definite competence-hit moment at the perfect tap. Avoids the live-motion-sandbox-no-arc trap: bounded 5-tap arc with named verdict at the end, not infinite-tap. The cat-letter is the share artifact — typewritten note in monospace = unmistakable Form. Recovers from today's three sci-fi rejections by going fully everyday-domestic. Premise legible in 3 seconds (one ASCII cat, the word 'tap'). Caption: 'the cat said i was acceptable'. LLM=light because the tone catalog is finite (~20 cat-judgments) and just gets one personalized closing line per outcome.

name: Telephone Brain
pitch: Two friends join via a four-letter room code on two phones. Player A is shown one tile from a hand-curated deck of 100 absurdly specific feelings ('the feeling of finding a 20 in last winter's coat'; 'the gap between the elevator stopping and the doors opening'). Player A composes a 4-emoji sequence on a constrained 60-emoji palette (no typing, no drawing). Player B receives only the emoji sequence and picks their guess from a shuffled 8-tile multiple-choice — one of which is the truth. Best of 5, swap roles each round. The shared-brain score across all 10 transmissions plots on the live histogram of every duo who's ever played, and you get a stamped pair-verdict: 'You and Sarah are an 87th-percentile shared-brain pair, classified by the Bureau of Synapse Telegraphy as A FUNCTIONALLY-LINKED LOBE PAIR — recommended for emergency séance work.'
rationale: Multiplayer is the single most under-built shape on the shelf — only Cartograph Duel (drawing) and Reflex Duel II (reaction time) are live, both physical-skill duels. A pure semantic-transmission duel is missing entirely. Specifically dodges One-Phone Charades Duel's failure (archived May 5) by replacing the 'tilt-for-drawing-clue + human judge' input model with a constrained emoji-palette sender + machine-graded multiple-choice receiver — no human arbitration friction. Dodges the mobile-draw wall (no drawing on glass — the suspicious-marks / sketch-trial / provenance-office cluster), the paragraph-input wall (no typing — the acquisitions-editor cluster), the recall-from-life wall (the tile deck is curated), and the wrapper-shape critique (no LLM in the receiver loop, just deterministic semantic distance against a known vocabulary). Histogram + pair-verdict is the validated Closer to 1.000 shape applied to a duo metric. Job-to-be-done stack: identity + connection — 'we are a shared-brain pair' is a caption that pulls the partner into the share, not just the user. Solo-UAT-able via two-phone test. Risk: the 60-emoji palette has to carry signal across 100 tiles — mitigation is to over-design the deck-encoding pairing so each tile has 3+ plausible emoji compositions, sample-tested solo before promote. Differentiates from Reflex Duel II (which is reaction speed only — no inter-player comprehension) and from Cartograph Duel (drawing geometry, not meaning).
description: A two-phone duo game administered by the Bureau of Synapse Telegraphy: encode absurdly specific feelings as 4-emoji ciphers from a 60-symbol palette and receive a stamped pair-verdict — your shared-brain score plotted on the live cross-duo histogram.

name: Texting Decoder
description: Reply to six rapid-fire texts the way you actually would (hey wyd, did u eat, cancel plans without being rude…). The app analyzes punctuation, capitalization, emoji use, abbreviations, and reply length to deterministically assign a named texting archetype — 'The Lowercase Romantic', 'Captain Capslock', 'The Ellipsis Poet', 'The "lol" Linguist', etc. The result shows your actual replies quoted as iMessage-style bubbles with annotated tells, ready to screenshot. Seeded: same 6 replies always yield the same archetype. Pastel-zine aesthetic with Archivo Black display type.

name: The Acquisitions Editor
description: Type one paragraph pitching your weirdest niche interest; a jaded mid-list publishing editor writes back a 4-line rejection-or-acquisition letter on your idea, with an absurd advance figure ($1.18 to $9,840) and a 'comp title' nobody's heard of.

name: The Bullwhip
description: A solo, two-minute Beer Game run rendered as four pixel-art warehouses stacked vertically — Retailer, Distributor, Wholesaler, Factory — connected by a conveyor of cardboard cases. The user picks one tier on the title card; the other three are AI agents driven by an anchoring-and-adjustment heuristic. Each tick the user taps how many cases to order from upstream. A hidden customer-demand curve has one small bump at week 3. After 20 weeks the Bureau of Logistical Conduct issues a deadpan Bullwhip Audit: a ripple chart of orders across all four tiers, peak inventory, stockout weeks, and a named manager archetype. Same demand seed for everyone today; archetype keyed off (variance, lag, peak-inventory). Share replays the exact 20 ticks via URL fragment.

name: The Cabinet Briefing
description: Six chunky toggles and dials styled as 1960s war-room control panel knobs (defense posture, monetary tightness, immigration mood, climate-cope, vibes economy, public optimism). Set the policy mix, then tap "BRIEF THE PRESIDENT." Receive an LLM-generated official Presidential Daily Brief — three news bulletins from your alternate timeline that feel oddly plausible, each tied to a specific dial setting (e.g. "PETROLEUM REGIME (medium-low) — strategic pelican reserve releases 14% to offset diner-coffee inflation"). Stamped "EYES ONLY," fake redaction bars, manilla cover. Change one dial → regenerate just the relevant bulletin. Share = URL fragment encoding the dial settings, recipient sees your exact alternate-timeline brief.

name: The Eavesdropper
description: Drop into a cozy fictional cafe and listen in on five passing conversations between strangers. Tap to follow whichever voice intrigues you — the cafe's ambient layout, who you sat near, and which fragments you lingered on become the input. Output is a short hand-typed letter from one of the strangers, addressed to *you*, claiming you eavesdropped on a moment that mattered. Different seat → different letter. No typing required.

name: The FOBO Simulator
description: Watch your pixel-art job get slowly replaced by an AI robot in real time — tap to fight back with increasingly desperate upskilling attempts. The robot always wins. At the end, you get an official Obsolescence Certificate naming the AI that replaced you and the absurd cause of displacement.

name: The Met Gala Step-and-Repeat
pitch: User answers 5 absurd quick-tap chip questions about their week (mood, breakfast, conflict, song stuck in head, recurring dream) and gets escorted down a fake red-carpet hallway as paparazzi flashes pop. At the end: a fashion-critic verdict card with a named look ('Distressed Cathedral by the House of Tuesday'), the user's outfit dossier, and a one-line review in the voice of a snarky Vogue commentator. Output is a styled gala-arrival ID badge / press-pass artifact with their look-name, gown house, and verdict score on a 1-100 'Cultural Resonance' scale.
rationale: Lands in the genuinely empty navigate × archetype-reveal cell. Borrows the Met Gala (May 4) cultural moment with a one-week lift window — timely without being a clone. Solves the wizard-depth watchlist by collapsing 5 chip-taps into a single navigate-down-the-carpet animation (~30s total). Five chip axes give input-resolution coupling enough lift to clear the hard rejection rule. LLM writes one personalized critic sentence as a payoff, not as the medium of the experience. Premise legible in 5s ('what would your Met Gala arrival look like'). Stance: mock-fashion-critic, matching the petty-small-claims success register. Every named look is flattering-absurd. Solo-UAT-able single-player journey; mobile-native chip-tap navigation.

name: The Standing Ovation Audit
description: A faux awards ceremony plays absurd categories ('Best Apology Heard At Brunch', 'Lifetime Achievement in Reply-All'). The user clap-taps with variable intensity (hold for thunder, single tap for polite golf-clap). Their clap pattern across 8 categories produces a deadpan letter from 'The Academy of Polite Disappointment' judging which categories they'd applaud and what their selectivity reveals. Output is a stamped Academy letter, screenshottable, mock-bureaucratic voice.

name: The Sundown Line
