pitch: A live world map showing the terminator — the line where day becomes night right now. Tap any city to read a single sentence about its dusk this minute.
rationale: Extends the observe×daily-reveal hot streak (Tonight's Sky, Tide Diviner, Pocket Telescope all active and scoring). Pure solar-position math — no API auth needed, deterministic from current UTC. Awe-arousal handle (scale, transformation) per Berger & Milkman. Light LLM adds one personalized sentence per tapped city; the terminator math is the irreducible core (Pitfall 7 prompt-equivalence defense). Striking globe-with-wave-of-night screenshot fits aggregator-frontpage rule.

name: The Tuner
description: Six labeled knobs (FREQ, DECAY, HARMONICS, GLOOM, FERAL, NOSTALGIA) on a dark instrument console. As you turn each, a live monospace readout panel updates in real time — the broadcast persona name at the top morphs word-by-word, the waveform under it changes shape, and tiny side-units (kHz / MK / Kp-style numerics) tick. Commit to lock it in: you get a named broadcast persona ("Pirate Radio of Suburban Grief"), a one-paragraph dispatch from that station (LLM-personalized over the slider state), and a stamped "TRANSMISSION LICENCE" card to share. The knob positions encode in the share URL so friends open the same station.

name: The Volcano You Built
pitch: Tap anywhere on a flat island to drop heat. Heat above threshold ignites neighbors, plates buckle, and an emergent volcanic ridge grows from your tap pattern. After 60 seconds the camera pulls back and reveals a satellite-style portrait of YOUR volcano with a name derived from your tap geography ('Mt. Slow-Burn West-Face,' 'Tri-Cone Smolder'). Steam vents continue animating in the share card.
rationale: Lands in tap-game/simulation (0 archived, 1 live — fresh). Avoids the heavy tap-game/score-stats and tap-game/archetype-reveal archive zones. Clear authorship (your taps shaped this), informational feedback (heat propagation visible), hard 60s session ceiling. Named landform + screenshot-ready aerial view is share-card legible at thumbnail size. Tap → heat → terrain is two-step but the intermediate (glowing heat) is rendered explicitly, satisfying the visualised-intermediate rule.
description: Tap a flat island to drop heat. Heat propagates, plates buckle, and a volcanic ridge grows from your tap pattern. After 60 seconds the camera pulls back to a satellite portrait with a name derived from your tap geography (e.g. 'Mt. Hard-Bake Tri-Cone NE-SW') and animating steam vents.

name: The Walking Tour Confession
description: A fake AI surveillance van follows you on a procedural pixel-art map for 90 seconds. You navigate by clicking 8-10 numbered street corners (the route IS the input — diner > pawn shop > vape store > dog park > ATM). At each stop the screen pauses and a deadpan plainclothes detective dictates a single line into your case file about what happened there. At the end you receive a stamped Surveillance Report: a named civilian-archetype verdict, the full route map as Exhibit A, and 8 numbered detective notes quoting your route choices back. Shareable: the recipient sees your exact route + report, then clicks through their own.

name: Their Color
description: Type a name and get a single bespoke color hand-named after them — rendered as a Pantone-style paint chip. Add a second name for a couple-color midpoint blended in OKLab. Save the chip as a PNG, share the link, and stack a growing palette of your friend group.

name: Tide Diviner
description: Pick any coastal city and see the next 14 days of real tides render as a hand-stamped almanac strip — chunky monospace tide chart, peak/trough markers, moon-phase glyphs, and a daily one-line forecast verdict per day ("Tue: spring tide, do not fish for opinions"). Tap any day to expand its panel (tide height, time-to-next-high, moon phase, sun angle). Toggle 12 lenses (tide / moon / sunrise-sunset / SST / currents / swell / spring-neap / lunar-illumination / ISS-pass / wind / pressure / the-dock-cat-says) — each lens is a fresh screenshot of the same almanac. Permalink encodes city + lens. Live data via no-key Open-Meteo Marine; pure-client computation otherwise. The page IS the share.

name: Tonight's Sky
description: Geolocate (or pick a city) and see tonight's sky overhead in 12 toggleable lenses — visible, planets+ecliptic, constellations, Bortle/light-pollution, ISS passes, deep-sky targets, Milky Way arc, meteor radiants, satellite tracks, lunar detail, equatorial grid, names off. A 60-night calendar grid below shows moon phase + best target per night. Pure-client computed astronomy (Meeus + Schlyter); instrument-credibility aesthetic.

name: Trace the Glyph
pitch: An unfamiliar glyph flashes for 3 seconds, then disappears. You trace it from memory. Get a precision score and a verdict: 'The Calligrapher,' 'The Approximator,' 'The Liar.'
rationale: Targets the empty draw×score-stats sparse cell. Memory-then-draw is a mechanic chat cannot reproduce (Pitfall 7 defense via input modality + scoring). Daily-glyph framing means everyone has the same target so scores compare directly — appreciation + controversy sub-types stack. Hausdorff-distance scoring is deterministic and runs offline; no LLM dependency, no auth, no copyrighted media.

name: Two Octaves
pitch: A single sine tone glides slowly upward in pitch. Tap the moment you think it has risen exactly one octave from where it started. Three rounds, increasing baseline-pitch difficulty. The app measures your absolute deviation in cents from the true octave, computes percentile against a static reference distribution, and stamps your verdict: 'Perfect Pitch / Trained Ear / Civilian / Tone Deaf, Affectionately.' Share card is a tiny waveform with your tap-line marked, plus the percentile.
rationale: Audio-first apps are nearly absent from the live shelf — the closest neighbors are visual-perception tests (Trace the Glyph) and reflex tests (Reflex Duel II), and neither involves a sound the doing of which IS the experience. Perceptual psychophysics has a built-in 'how did it know?' eerie-accuracy hook. No AI, no copyrighted audio (procedural sine sweep), no wrapper risk, no recall-from-life input, no draw-on-mobile, no multi-screen wizard. Mobile-fits cleanly: one button, one tap, three rounds in 30 seconds. Solo-UAT passes by design: replay-driven score-improvement loop. Verdict desirability holds: even 'Tone Deaf, Affectionately' is wear-with-pride. Risk: needs reliable mobile-Safari Web Audio (handle silently-muted iPhones with a one-tap 'unlock audio' intro). Differentiator from Reflex Duel: this measures a perceptual judgment, not raw motor reaction.
description: Audio-first psychoacoustic test: a sine tone climbs upward, you tap when you think it's risen exactly one octave — three rounds, named verdict, percentile against a static reference distribution.

name: Vibe Tax Calculator
description: Enter a vibe as plain text (e.g. 'Coachella influencer', 'dark academia TA', 'VC at a hackathon'). The app computes and returns an itemized 'Vibe Tax' receipt: line items like 'espresso martinis — $47', 'performative book — $22', 'lingering vape cloud — $3.50', totaling a surprising dollar figure plus a sassy auditor verdict. Deterministic on input. Presented as a crumpled thermal-printer receipt graphic — instantly screenshot-able.

name: The Voicemail You Never Sent
pitch: Pick a single chip — who you almost called (your ex / your mom / your boss / your sixth-grade teacher / a number you no longer have / 911 by accident). Then tilt your phone like you're holding it to your ear. The screen goes near-black, an LLM-written 30-second voicemail transcript appears one line at a time as if you're whispering it, and at the end snaps into a stylized 'unsent voicemail' artifact — iPhone-Voicemail-screenshot aesthetic with timestamp, duration, transcript, and a hand-stamped 'NEVER SENT' watermark.
rationale: Lands in tilt-rotate × letter-narrative (0/0 — completely untried) and tilt-rotate has 0 archived across every cell so the substrate has real headroom. Phone-to-ear gesture is a one-step monotonic metaphor with universal cultural reference (everyone has done this with their phone) — clears the device-orientation-controls bar because the listener IS the metaphor, not a parameter. Includes the 'wait for first non-null orientation reading' fix from the phantom-putt update. Single chip + one gesture = no wizard depth, no paragraph labor. Output is a stylized voicemail-transcript artifact (document-cert-shaped), not bare archetype text — clears the bare-text-archetype watchlist. Arousal: anxiety + parasocial tenderness, both research-backed sharers. iPhone-voicemail-screenshot aesthetic is an instantly meme-template-shaped Form (polysemic: shareable earnestly OR ironically). Wrapper test passes (multi-step gesture + chip + LLM payload conditioned on both, not single-shot). Avoids both sci-fi register AND the the-eavesdropper failure (AI text is the payoff for an authored gesture, not the medium of the experience).

name: Weather God Mode
description: A pixel-art coastal town under a live sky. Tap clouds to grow them, hold to spark lightning, double-tap to release rain. Keep tapping past the cap and the cloud locks into a thunderhead — anvil-shaped and dim — at which point hold spawns a thicker thunder-bolt with a rumbling screen shake, and double-tap dumps hail that crushes ripe crops and scatters townsfolk through their umbrellas. The townsfolk visibly react in real time — umbrellas pop, crops sprout, picnics flee, lighthouse keepers wave thanks. After 60 seconds the Meteorological Society of the Imagined Coast issues your stamped 'Divinity Audit' — a named weather-god archetype ('Petty Drought-Lord of the Tomato Patch', 'Baptismal Flooder, 3rd Class', 'Marshal of Sudden Hail', 'Quartermaster of the Apocalypse', 'The Lightning-Shy Mercy God') keyed deterministically off the actual interventions you performed (lightning, thunder pulses, rain volume, hail volume, thunderheads summoned, sustained pressure, percent of town affected). Share artifact is a screenshot of the chaos at peak intensity with the verdict overlaid + a single deadpan caption from the meteorologist on duty.

name: Weather By Hostage Note
description: Pick any of 80 world cities and the atmosphere returns its 3-day forecast as a cut-out-magazine ransom note — every letter a styled DOM span with seeded rotations, mismatched serif/sans fonts, tape strips, and numbered demands. Forecast pulled live from Open-Meteo (no key); same city on the same day deterministically yields the identical note, shareable via a #fragment URL.

name: Weather Maze
description: Enter your city and today's Open-Meteo weather data seeds a unique procedural maze — warm sunny days produce wide-open labyrinths, stormy days spawn dense twisting corridors. Solve it with arrow keys or swipe, then share your completion time and today's weather-generated maze thumbnail as a spoiler-free emoji map. A new maze generates each day per city.

name: What Flavor of Burned Out Are You
description: A 10-question absurdist burnout-diagnosis quiz. Result is a named burnout archetype with a deadpan fake-clinical prognosis and AI-generated treatment plan.

name: What MySpace Profile Were You?
description: A generator that takes your birth year, music taste, and a few personality prompts to produce a fake MySpace profile snapshot — complete with your 'Top 8' archetypes, profile song genre, About Me tone, and a named 2000s internet persona. Visual output designed to be screenshotted.

name: What's Your Corporate Archetype?
description: A quiz that analyzes your workplace instincts through absurdly specific office-life scenarios and assigns you one of ~25 irreverent corporate archetypes — 'The Synergy Vampire', 'The Calendar Blocker', 'The Reply-All Anarchist'. Results are deterministic (same answers = same archetype every time) and designed to be hilariously accurate for anyone who has worked in an office.

name: Which Crew Are You
pitch: Twelve mostly-photo questions about your apartment, your phone, your fridge — pick the image closest to yours. The ship assigns you to one of nine specific roles on a derelict hauler ('Coolant Auditor', 'Night Shift Kelp Tech', 'Voluntary Hibernator'), each with a one-sentence dossier and a stamped crew badge. Every role is a place someone would actually want to be assigned.
rationale: configure/archetype-reveal is sparse (1 archived, 0 live), sidestepping the heavily oversaturated text-input/archetype-reveal cell while still hitting the highest-virality format (identity quiz). The 'image-pick' input is a configure mechanic that breaks out of typing fatigue. Verdict-desirability test passes by design — every role is named to be claimed, not feared (no 'Threat Level: HIGH'). LLM only writes the one personalized closing sentence per dossier. Solo-UAT, deterministic, fits the spaceship steering, and the archetype name doubles as a Reddit-post-friendly title ('I'm the ship's Voluntary Hibernator').

name: Which Houseplant Are You Killing
description: Three taps about your apartment's light, your watering habits, and your weekly schedule. The verdict is the specific houseplant you'd inevitably murder, with a flattering archetype name for the kind of plant-killer you are ('The Overwaterer of Monstera', 'The Dry-Spell Aristocrat'). Result card has a hand-drawn pot-of-bones and one sentence describing exactly how the plant dies in your care.

name: Wiki Tunnel
description: Daily Wikipedia race: everyone gets the same start and end article. Click only links inside Wikipedia pages to get from one to the other. Your click count earns a named verdict (Synapse Sniper / Tunnel Visionary / Tangent Tourist / Lost Wanderer) based on how close to the optimal-known path you got. Share card encodes the day's seed and your route as a 4-icon trail.

name: Word Duel
description: Two players race to build the longest word from a shared pool of 12 random letters. Each player types their best word in 90 seconds; longest valid word wins.

name: You Da Birthday
description: A birthday destiny calculator — enter your birthday and get your absurd cosmic role.

name: Your Commute, Simulated
description: Tap your commute type (subway, bus, walk, car, wfh) and commute length in minutes. A procedural side-scrolling pixel-art simulation of your commute plays out — a cast of fellow commuters with behavioral quirks enact a 60-second micro-drama. At the end, a commute archetype stamp is revealed based on the cast interactions. Shareable via URL fragment.
